thread:
oncall-alex: Pager: multi-gpu serving pool 'rp-nd-48' reported repeated NCCL TIMEOUTs and one CUDA kernel crash, multiple containers restarting. Auto-escalating to incidents channel. @sre-jordan @eng-runtime-lee :rotating_light:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1845678901 - nccl: detected 3 TIMEOUT events within 2m on pool rp-nd-48. Severity: P1. Pager sent to oncall-alex.
oncall-alex: seeing GPU0/3 showing 'NCCL WARN TIMEOUT' in logs and container exit with 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION'.
eng-runtime-lee: copying logs now, do not restart pods until we capture /var/log/nccl*out. Might be KV cache corruption after an OOM.
sre-jordan: any customer impact?
oncall-alex: yes — two dedicated jobs on rp-nd-48 (tenant: big-ml-recs-prod) saw degraded allreduce latency -> retries -> failed requests. CS notified.
customer-success-maya: I've pinged the customer and told them we're investigating; they reported failed inferences and increased tail latency ~09:12 UTC.
infra-kate: nodes node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-18 flapped network briefly at 09:08, kernel logs show NIC reset. Could be causing NCCL communicator tears.
eng-runtime-lee: interesting. NCCL communicator timeouts often follow link flaps. We should probe whether the communicator IDs changed mid-job. Can we capture nv_peer_mem and iptables?
oncall-ryan: oncall rotating in 10m. @oncall-alex handing off after we stabilize.
eng-runtime-lee: dump of recent nccl logs (redacted):
```
[09:11:53] NCCL WARN Call 0x7f8b5c: Allreduce() timeout after 120s
[09:11:54] NCCL INFO Communicator 0x3e1a lost rank 2
[09:11:54] CUDA ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION at ./kernel.cu:214
[09:12:01] Process 24321 exited with code 139
```
sre-jordan: can we repro on a warm-up job? Or should we evacuate workloads off the two nodes while we root cause?
eng-runtime-lee: immediate mitigation: 1) cordon node-gpu-17/18 2) drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data 3) set NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0 for the next restart to avoid GPUDirect issues 4) restart affected jobs on alternate pool.
oncall-alex: doing step 1/2 now.
infra-kate: cordoned both nodes. starts draining node-gpu-17 -> pods evicting.
oncall-alex: running: kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n serving || true
eng-runtime-lee: when restarting, add env var in the deployment: "NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1" and "NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0" temporarily. Also enable "NCCL_DEBUG=INFO" to collect more detail.
sre-jordan: note for RCA: we should capture tc qdisc stats and check for MTU mismatches. Infra — can you pull switch port flaps?
infra-kate: grabbed switch logs — port 2 on rack-7 shows 09:07:58 carrier loss for ~30s, then came back. Pushing to network team.
eng-runtime-lee: ok, applying temporary rollout to scale down batch size to avoid kv-cache blowouts while we redeploy.
oncall-alex: pods from big-ml-recs-prod are being rescheduled to rp-nd-32 and rp-nd-16. One instance failed to start due to CUDA driver mismatch, patching node selectors.
oncall-ryan: taking over oncall; @oncall-alex drop me a quick warm handoff when you have a sec.
oncall-alex: handoff: observed 3x NCCL TIMEOUTs, 1x CUDA_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION causing SIGSEGV; nodes had NIC flaps; cordoned nodes; draining; redeploying jobs to rp-nd-32 with NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0, NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. CS notified, customer degraded but recovery in progress.
customer-success-maya: customer confirms traffic routed to alternate cluster, seeing improved success rate. Asking for ETA on full recovery.
eng-runtime-lee: ETA to confirm stable: 30-45m after all pods are back and no further NCCL warnings in logs. We'll collect per-token latency percentiles.
sre-jordan: creating incident ticket: INC-2026-1845678901. Adding initial notes and assigning to eng-runtime for RCA.
eng-runtime-lee: collecting core dumps and nvml stats: running gcore on process ids, saving to /mnt/incident/cores. Also enabling trace via NCCL_TRACE=1 for the next run.
oncall-alex: Uploading logs to incident bucket: gs://redwood-incident-logs/1845678901/ — nccl.log, docker.log, dmesg.txt.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] Channel: incidents; Incident INC-2026-1845678901 created by sre-jordan; severity P1; status: mitigation in progress.
infra-kate: network team confirms a partial fiber reroute at 09:07 that may have caused momentary packet loss to rack-7. They've scheduled follow-up and assert link is stable now.
eng-runtime-lee: follow-ups for RCA: 1) correlate SDK-level per-step latencies vs network flaps 2) check whether kernel upgrade on node-gpu-18 changed NV driver behavior 3) determine if KV cache corruption can lead to illegal instruction after reattach.
oncall-ryan: will monitor for 1h and then if stable downgrade to sev2. If errors spike again, escalate to infra and consider pool quarantine.
customer-success-maya: customer requests postmortem and confirmation of mitigation actions. I'll coordinate timeline and notify them when RCA is available.
eng-runtime-lee: quick command we ran to toggle GDR off on a deployment (example):
```
kubectl set env deploy/recs-worker NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0 -n big-ml-recs-prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/recs-worker -n big-ml-recs-prod
```
oncall-alex: all affected pods restarted on alternate nodes. No new NCCL TIMEOUTs seen in the last 6m.
sre-jordan: marking node-gpu-17/18 quarantine. We'll keep cordoned until network team signs off.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE CHECK] No new alerts in 15m. Lets verify logs for 30m before closing.
oncall-ryan: handing back to @oncall-alex for follow-up and RCA.
oncall-alex: ack. I'll collect artifacts, write RCA draft and attach to INC-2026-1845678901. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
eng-runtime-lee: adding note: after RCA we should consider defaulting to NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 for workloads with long-lived communicators, and add an automated pod relocation policy on repeated NCCL WARNs.
customer-success-maya: customer asked if we can add a playbook for them on transient failures — will propose a runbook entry.
eng-runtime-lee: saving final logs: /mnt/incident/1845678901/final.tar.gz
noncall-alex: last check-in: no regressions for 30m — leaving incident open for follow-up tasks.
